overall: The AG found the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law: its February 4, 2020 executive session under Purpose 3 on the Housatonic settlement was properly noticed and convened, and public participation was the chair's call. No order issued.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Board secretly deliberated and approved the Housatonic River settlement without an open meeting, in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: We also find that the executive session discussions were appropriate under Purpose 3 because they related to pending litigation and a settlement agreement that was a proposed resolution to that litigation.

allegations.summary: Complainants challenged the sufficiency of the February 4 meeting notice's executive session topic and the procedural steps taken before convening in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: First, we find that the Board provided sufficient detail in its meeting notice with respect to the executive session topic and complied with the required procedural steps prior to convening in executive session on February 4.

allegations.summary: Complainants argued the settlement approval had to be announced or ratified in open session rather than voted on behind closed doors.
allegations.key_passage: The Board was not required, as the complaints suggest, to announce or ratify the settlement agreement in open session where the Board convened in executive session under Purpose 3 and not under Purpose 9.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the public was not allowed to participate in the settlement approval.
allegations.key_passage: Thus, it is not a violation of the law if the chair decides not to allow any public participation during a meeting.

allegations.summary: One complainant suggested the Board improperly met in executive session on Housatonic matters in fall 2018; the AG declined a broad audit but checked minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Our office will not conduct broad audits of public bodies.
